summary: This Makefile defines a set of convenient commands for working with a Docker container called 'dagger_daemon'. It sets up variables for the daemon name and Docker socket access, then creates shortcuts to build the image and run it with different entry points — whether you want an interactive bash shell, help documentation, or to run linting checks.

explanations.2: This stores a Docker volume mount flag as a variable so we can reuse it in multiple commands; it gives the container access to the host machine's Docker daemon through a Unix socket file.
explanations.4: .PHONY tells Make that 'build' is not a real file we're trying to create, just a command label, so Make won't get confused if a file named 'build' exists.
explanations.6: This builds a Docker image from the Dockerfile located at .docker/Dockerfile and tags it with the name stored in DAEMON_NAME, using the current directory as the build context.
explanations.10: This runs the Docker container interactively with a bash shell as the entry point; the flags mount the Docker socket (so the container can access Docker), mount the current directory into /app/src, and clean up the container when done.
explanations.14: Similar to bash, this runs the container but executes 'call --help' instead, showing documentation for what commands the daemon supports.
explanations.18: This runs the container with the 'call lint' command to execute a linting check inside the containerized environment.
